programme: SMARCC1, L3MBTL1, and HINFP converge on chromatin control of the RB1/E2F–cyclin–CDK2 entry into S-phase: SMARCC1 (a core SWI/SNF/BAF subunit) targets its own complex partners SMARCB1 and SMARCA4 alongside KRAS, L3MBTL1 (an MBT-domain chromatin-compaction reader) targets the cell-cycle genes MYC, CCNE1, and RUNX1, and HINFP targets the histone-biogenesis/G1-S axis directly through CDK2, NPAT, and RB1. Together they read as chromatin opening (SWI/SNF) versus compaction (L3MBTL1) at proliferation genes, coupled to histone supply (HINFP-NPAT) for the cells that pass the checkpoint.
role_in_a: Chromatin-complex dysregulation is a recurrent theme in clear cell renal carcinoma. SMARCC1 has direct record here (33532313: expression tracks pathological grade, with a mixed grade/prognosis relationship), and its targeting of SMARCB1 and SMARCA4 fits control of BAF complex stoichiometry alongside KRAS. L3MBTL1 and HINFP have no disease-specific record and would only be expected, not shown, to gate the same MYC/CCNE1/RB1 proliferative genes.
role_in_b: None of the three has documented support in multiple sclerosis. HINFP carries a comparatively high Open Targets percentile (0.92) but its one retrieved paper concerns neurological disorders and type 2 diabetes, not clearly multiple sclerosis, and ReMap shows no observed binding at any of its nine listed targets — so even indirect binding evidence is absent. Any role for this trio in lymphocyte clonal expansion during autoimmune attack is inferred from general cell-cycle biology, not from anything retrieved.
shared_axis: If this axis is real, it would be that ccRCC tumor-cell division and antigen-driven expansion of autoreactive lymphocytes in MS both pass through the same chromatin/histone-supply gate on S-phase entry. That mechanism, however, is generic to almost any proliferating cell type and is not something specific to kidney or brain tissue, which weakens it as an explanation for why these two particular diseases would share it.
reasoning: The three factors form a nameable chromatin/cell-cycle circuit rather than an arbitrary list, and kidney and brain have no anatomical or clinical link that would make the pairing obvious, which fits 'unexpected'. But the record only places one factor (SMARCC1) in one disease with an ambiguous directionality, L3MBTL1 has zero record in either disease, and HINFP's sole retrieved paper is off-topic with no supporting ReMap binding — so the account rests almost entirely on generic cell-cycle reasoning rather than retrieved evidence, which caps it at weak.
support: 33532313 — SMARCC1 expression correlates with pathological grade and (paradoxically) with good prognosis in clear cell renal carcinoma, the only direct placement of any carrying factor in either disease. No reliable support for L3MBTL1 or HINFP: L3MBTL1 returned no papers in either disease; HINFP's one retrieved paper (32041280) discusses neurological disorders and type 2 diabetes comorbidities and does not clearly reference multiple sclerosis.
how_to_falsify: ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq for SMARCC1, L3MBTL1, and HINFP in ccRCC tumor cells versus activated MS-relevant lymphocytes (e.g., TH17 or clonally expanded CD4+ T cells) at the RUNX1/CCNE1/MYC/CDK2/NPAT/RB1 loci: if the factors do not co-occupy these loci in the lymphocyte context, or occupancy in ReMap-type data (already null for HINFP's nine targets) stays null on retest, the shared checkpoint story fails. A cleaner single test: knock down HINFP or L3MBTL1 in a ccRCC line and in activated primary T/B cells in parallel — if proliferation is affected in only one cell type, the axis is not shared.
caveats: Brain and kidney share no direct anatomy or clinical overlap, so any connection here must run through a cell-intrinsic proliferation mechanism rather than tissue biology. The 390 patient-group comparisons draw on only 6 independent cohort pairs, so the comparisons are clustered, not fully independent replicates. The tissue-generic exclusion list is dominated by neural/immune master regulators (MEF2C, FOXP3, STAT4, TCF4, ASCL1, DLX5, HES6), meaning tissue-driven concordance was already stripped out before this list was built — what remains is a narrower signal, but also one without an obvious tissue-level explanation to fall back on. Several chromatin-related factors (RCOR1, ATRX, KAT6B) appear in the single-view exclusion list, showing that chromatin regulators surfaced in individual patient groups but mostly failed to generalize, which is consistent with the concordant chromatin trio here being a modest, borderline signal rather than a strong one.
